merger_name: Syngenta Crop Protection and Dümmen Orange – Joint Venture Formation
merger_description:
Syngenta Crop Protection AG (**SCPAG**) and the Dümmen Orange Group (**Dümmen Orange**) propose to enter a joint venture to combine their global ornamental plant breeding and propagation businesses.

SCPAG is a Swiss agribusiness that operates in the crop protection and seeds markets in Australia and internationally. In Australia, SCPAG operates through its wholly owned subsidiary, Syngenta APP Assets, selling and distributing seeds for annuals, perennials, and pot plants.

Dümmen Orange is a global horticultural company that operates in breeding and propagation of flowers and plants. In Australia, Dümmen Orange’s primary activity is the licensing of plant genetics under the Dümmen Orange brand. Dümmen Orange also supplies cuttings and in vitro materials for annuals, perennials, pot plants and cut flowers.

events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Syngenta Crop Protection AG (SCPAG) and the Dümmen Orange
Group (Dümmen Orange) propose to enter a joint venture to
combine their global ornamental plant breeding and propagation
businesses (the Joint Venture).
The Joint Venture will be formed by Watson BidCo B.V. (Dümmen
Orange SPV) (holding 50.1% of the shares) and Syngenta Crop
Protection AG (SCPAG) (holding 49.9% of the shares) (together, the
Parties).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

SCPAG is a Swiss agribusiness that operates in the crop protection
and seeds markets in Australia and internationally. In Australia,
SCPAG operates through its wholly owned subsidiary, Syngenta APP
Assets (Syngenta APP), selling and distributing seeds for annuals,
perennials, and pot plants.
Dümmen Orange is a global horticultural company that operates in
breeding and propagation of flowers and plants. In Australia,
Dümmen Orange’s primary activity is the licensing of plant genetics
under the Dümmen Orange brand. Dümmen Orange also supplies
cuttings and in vitro materials for annuals, perennials, pot plants and
cut flowers.

The Parties overlap in the sale and distribution of ornamental plants,
annual and perennial potted plants and bedding plants for
propagation within Australia.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, publicly available information and information
from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following finding:
• the merged firm would continue to face competition from
alternative plant propagators and breeders in Australia.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
